newsitem.title: USA: Jailed American in N.Korea found homesick.
newsitem.headline: Jailed American in N.Korea found homesick.

text.p: An American being held in North Korea on spying charges is in good physical health but very low spirits and wants to go home, the State Department said on Tuesday.
The report came from Swedish diplomat Ake Lafquist who was permitted to visit Carl Hunziker, 26, on Nov. 8 and 9, deputy spokesman Glyn Davies told reporters.

Hunziker, described by his family as a missionary, was arrested in North Korea on Aug. 24 after entering from China. U.S. officials have ridiculed North Korean allegations that he is a spy and have demanded his release.

According to the Swedish consul, which represents U.S. interests in North Korea and have made several visits to the detained man, "Hunzinker appears to be in reasonably good physical health," Davies said.

But "he's in very, very low spirits. He expressed a strong desire to be allowed to go home as soon as possible, and we renew our call on the North Korean government to release him immediately and to allow him to come home," Davies added.

Hunziker was held for some time in a hotel in a town about four hours' train ride from the capital, Pyongyang. But he was transferred on Oct. 19 from the hotel to a detention centre, located between Pyongyang and Sinuiju, in northwestern North Korea, Davies said.

Hunziker was brought from the detention centre to a hotel in Sinuiju to meet the Swedish diplomat and thereafter was to be returned to the detention centre. U.S. officials say they do not know the exact location of the detention centre.
